Incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey tilts the tone more guarded than the baseline. SLOOS indicates foreign banks reported weaker demand for C&I loans and for construction and land development loans, with reasons for tightening tied to economic outlook and liquidity, while demand for nonfarm nonresidential and multifamily CRE was unchanged and some easing reflected competition. This mix corroborates the FOMC’s weakness in business fixed investment and suggests capex-sensitive credit demand remains soft, with supply not broadly easing. While the policy stance and money-market operations remain supportive, SLOOS points to more persistent investment headwinds. Netting these, the overall stance stays cautiously supportive but with greater caution around business credit and CRE development than previously assessed.
